question: The access: who may touch the Fed, and who holds a charter or license?
answer: This page reads every gate between crypto firms and the dollar system: the 36 institutions in the Fed-account and bank-charter queue, firm by firm (2 with a full master account, 1 with a limited account, 1 waiting, 1 in court); the 4 account types and what each allows; the queue counts; the 59-entry dated charter record; the legal routes map (26 jobs, 52 routes, 57 firms and public bodies); the 14 transition gates; the court cases on Fed accounts and on removing a Fed governor; and every legal placement. A charter and a Fed account are separate decisions by different agencies.

sections.title: All 36 institutions: Fed account and charter
sections.sub: Covers crypto, stablecoin and fintech firms in the charter/Fed-account queue plus the two non-crypto Tier 3 approvals (needed for the 3-of-53 count). Excludes non-crypto de novo banks (Mercury, Upstart, VALT, Augustus, Mission Lane, Avant, Stark, Itaú, bunq — bunq appears only in the denial count) and non-U.S. rails in charter.json (Fnality, Partior, Canton, Swift, DTCC items). 'additional_charters' and 'notes' are extra fields used where one firm holds two charters or needs a one-line caveat.

sections.part: 1 · Fed accounts and charters, firm by firm

rows.title: Kraken (Kraken Financial)
fields: Payward Financial, Inc., doing business as Kraken Financial (a Wyoming special purpose depository institution); parent Payward, Inc.
crypto exchange group with a state-chartered crypto bank (Wyoming SPDI)
Reserve bank: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

What it allows: Only the Fedwire Funds Service (large-value wire transfers), and only in a way that rejects any payment that would overdraw the account. No intraday credit, no discount-window loans, no interest on balances, and a cap on the end-of-day balance (amount not published). Only Kraken Financial may use it; the Kraken exchange and other Payward companies may not. Initial term of one year. Kraken told Reuters it also has no FedNow or ACH access. As of mid-July 2026 Kraken's CEO said the account was not yet operating; no later public evidence of use was found.

— Date: 2026-03-04; What: Kansas City Fed announces it approved a limited-purpose account for Kraken Financial, classified Tier 3, for an initial term of one year, with restrictions tailored to its business.
— Date: 2026-03-26; What: Rep. Maxine Waters asks the Kansas City Fed to explain the legal basis, services, limits and controls of the account.

— Date: 2026-05-08; What: Kansas City Fed publishes the account's restrictions: Fedwire Funds only, no intraday or discount-window credit, no interest, closing-balance limit, no access for other Payward companies; says it could be viewed as a pilot of the Payment Account concept.
— Date: 2026-05-20; What: Sen. Blunt Rochester asks the Board and Kansas City Fed for records on the approval.
— Date: 2026-06-18; What: ICBA asks the Kansas City Fed to review the account and consider limits, suspension, non-renewal or termination.
Regulator: OCC (applied); Wyoming Banking Board (current state charter)
Charter type: Applied for a national trust company charter (Payward National Trust Company); currently holds a Wyoming special purpose depository institution charter
Events: Date: 2026-05-08; What: Payward National Trust Company application received by the OCC (listed as pending on the OCC's digital-asset applications page).

When does the one-year term start and end? Official sources say only 'initial term of one year'. Library dates: database Jan 28, 2026 (would end ~Jan 28, 2027) vs announcement Mar 4, 2026 (library's fed_timeline assumes Mar 4, 2027). Unresolved.
Has the account carried a first payment since the July 2026 testimony? No public evidence found through 2026-10-19.
Amount of the closing-balance limit (not published).
Has the Board's May 20, 2026 request to pause Tier 3 decisions affected renewal?
When did Kraken Financial file its account request? Not found.
Regulator: Wyoming Banking Board · Charter type: Wyoming special purpose depository institution (state crypto bank; not federally insured) · Status: final approval · Final: 2020-09-16
The Kansas City Fed calls this a 'limited purpose account', not a master account; it says the decision did not create a new account category or widen who is legally eligible.

sources.label: Kraken blog — Payward files application for OCC national trust company

rows.title: Custodia Bank
fields: Custodia Bank, Inc., Cheyenne, Wyoming (Wyoming special purpose depository institution)
Reserve bank: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City
What it allows: Nothing: the request was denied in January 2023 and the denial still stands. Custodia's petition asking the Supreme Court to review the denial is pending.
— Date: 2020-10; What: Custodia applies to the Kansas City Fed for a master account.
— Date: 2022-06-07; What: Custodia sues the Board and Kansas City Fed over the delay.
— Date: 2023-01-27; What: The Board denies Custodia's application to become a member of the Federal Reserve System.
— Date: 2023-01; What: Kansas City Fed denies the master account request, applying the 2022 account guidelines.
— Date: 2024-03-29; What: District court rules for the Fed.
— Date: 2025-10-31; What: Tenth Circuit affirms: Reserve Banks may deny eligible institutions; eligibility is not entitlement.
— Date: 2026-03-13; What: Tenth Circuit denies rehearing.
— Date: 2026-05-29; What: Justice Gorsuch extends the petition deadline to July 11, 2026.
— Date: 2026-07-10; What: Custodia files its petition for certiorari (docketed July 14 as No. 26-62).
— Date: 2026-08-12; What: Amicus briefs filed Aug 12–13 (Blockchain Association; The Digital Chamber; Sen. Lummis and others).
— Date: 2026-10-13; What: The Board and the Kansas City Fed file briefs opposing Supreme Court review (after two deadline extensions).
Charter type: Wyoming special purpose depository institution (state crypto bank; not federally insured)
Date Custodia received its Wyoming SPDI charter (the Tenth Circuit says only that it was before October 2020).
Will the Supreme Court grant review? Distribution for conference not yet shown on the docket as of 2026-10-19.
Exact day of the Kansas City Fed's master account denial (opinion says January 2023).

rows.title: Anchorage Digital
fields: Anchorage Digital Bank, National Association (Sioux Falls, SD; OCC charter 25243)
Tier: Tier 3 (library; Anchorage says the guidelines put national trust banks without a Fed-regulated holding company in Tier 3)
Reserve bank: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis (Anchorage says it is a Fed member through Minneapolis; the request's Reserve Bank is not stated in the sources read)
What it allows: Nothing yet: the request is pending. Anchorage says it may stay undecided through year-end because of the Board's Tier 3 pause.
— Date: 2025-08-28; What: Anchorage's request appears in the Fed's access-request database (pending).
— Date: 2026-05-31; What: Library reading of the Fed database (currency date May 31, 2026): still pending.
— Date: 2026-07-29; What: Anchorage says its full master account request 'remains pending' and calls the proposed Payment Account 'no workable substitute'.
Charter type: National trust bank charter (custody and fiduciary business; no insured deposits and no lending); converted from a South Dakota trust company
Decision ids: OCC news release 2021-6, OCC charter 25243, SCL 2026-01 (operating agreement terminated)
— Date: 2021-01-13; What: OCC conditionally approves conversion of Anchorage Trust Company to Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A., with an operating agreement.
— Date: 2026-02-09; What: OCC terminates the 2021 operating agreement; the charter continues.
— Date: 2026-09-30; What: Listed on the OCC's active trust banks list (charter 25243).
Status in the Fed database's Aug 31, 2026 data (official page is JavaScript-only and could not be read here).
Which Reserve Bank is reviewing the request (Minneapolis is likely but not stated).

sections.part: 1 · Fed accounts and charters, firm by firm

rows.title: Master account (full Federal Reserve account)
fields: Institutions that are legally eligible under the Federal Reserve Act (mainly depository institutions and member banks), at the Reserve Bank's discretion. The Board's 2022 guidelines sort requests into three tiers: Tier 1 = federally insured institutions (lightest review); Tier 2 = not federally insured but supervised by a federal banking agency, with any holding company under Fed oversight; Tier 3 = not federally insured and not federally supervised at the bank or holding-company level (strictest review). Two appeals courts (Tenth Circuit in Custodia, 2025; Second Circuit in Banco San Juan, 2026) held that eligibility does not create a right to an account, and an account can be taken away.

Payment services: Value: Yes; Note: Full access to Reserve Bank services such as Fedwire Funds, Fedwire Securities, FedACH, FedNow, the National Settlement Service and cash services, subject to each service's terms.
Interest on reserves: Value: Yes; Note: Eligible institutions earn interest on reserve balances.
Discount window: Value: Yes; Note: Depository institutions can borrow from the discount window if they meet its credit and collateral rules.
Intraday credit: Value: Yes; Note: Daytime overdrafts are allowed within caps under the Fed's Payment System Risk policy.

Federal Reserve Act (Reserve Banks 'may' receive deposits, 12 U.S.C. 342; Monetary Control Act pricing and access, 12 U.S.C. 248a); Board Guidelines for Evaluating Account and Services Requests (Aug 15, 2022); Reserve Bank Operating Circular 1. Buying Federal Reserve Bank stock (membership), which the OCC requires of new national trust banks, is a separate step and does not by itself give an account.
The Board's May 2026 proposal would also revise these guidelines; the final form is not yet published.

Discount window: Value: No; Note: No discount-window credit.
Intraday credit: Value: No; Note: No intraday credit; end-of-day balance is capped (amount not published).

rows.title: Special-purpose Payment Account (proposed)
fields: Any institution legally eligible for a Reserve Bank account, whatever its tier; an institution could not hold both a Payment Account and a master account. Reserve Banks would decide requests, generally within 90 days of a complete file. The proposal does not widen legal eligibility.

Payment services: Value: partial; Note: Only services where overdrafts can be rejected automatically: Fedwire Funds, FedNow, the National Settlement Service, and Fedwire Securities transfers free of payment. No FedACH and no securities delivery-versus-payment.
Interest on reserves: Value: No; Note: No interest on balances (Regulation D proposal).
Discount window: Value: No; Note: No discount-window credit (Regulation A proposal).
Intraday credit: Value: No; Note: No intraday credit. End-of-day balance capped at a level set per institution, at most $1 billion; no limit on balances during the day.

Proposed new Part IV of the Fed's Payment System Risk policy and revised Account Access Guidelines (Docket OP-1878, Federal Register 2026-10375, 91 FR 30627), with amendments to Regulation D (2026-10377) and Regulation A (2026-10376). Board approved May 20, 2026; published May 26, 2026; comments closed July 27, 2026. The Board asked Reserve Banks to pause Tier 3 decisions until it finishes. Preceded by a Dec 23, 2025 request for information.

sections.part: 2 · The dated charter record and Fed-access filings

rows.title: Fnality International is established
fields: A private company limited by shares, England and Wales, owned by a consortium of banks and market utilities. Its purpose is the one thing no stablecoin can offer: a settlement asset that *is* central-bank money, held in a pooled omnibus account at the Bank of England.

rows.title: Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A. receives the first digital-asset national trust charter
fields: OCC; Anchor Labs; Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.

The OCC charters the first national trust bank built for digital assets, under a 2021 operating agreement. Five years later it is still the only member of the cohort that has been a chartered, operating national bank the whole way through. A trust charter is not a commercial-bank charter: no insured deposits, no lending, no discount window, and no Federal Reserve master account.

rows.title: Partior is founded by DBS, J.P. Morgan and Temasek
fields: Partior; DBS; J.P. Morgan; Temasek; Standard Chartered

Out of the Monetary Authority of Singapore's Project Ubin. The settled asset is tokenized **commercial-bank money** — a liability of the participating settlement bank, not of Partior, and not of any central bank. Whoever the money is owed by is the whole question.

rows.title: The sterling Fnality Payment System is recognized as a UK payment system
fields: Fnality UK Limited; HM Treasury; Bank of England

Formal recognition. The pooled central-bank funds sit in trust in a Bank of England RTGS omnibus account. This is the only place in the whole sweep where a private tokenized rail settles in genuine central-bank money — and it took an act of national recognition to get there.

rows.title: The sterling Fnality system makes its first payments
fields: Fnality UK Limited; Lloyds; Santander; UBS
Three banks, an initial proving phase. Live — in the narrowest of the five senses of that word.

rows.title: Canton Coin genesis
fields: Canton Network; Canton Foundation; Digital Asset
No premine, no presale, no founder or venture allocation. The network is not owned by the company that builds its technology — a distinction the sweep insists on and most reporting collapses.

rows.title: The sterling Fnality system operates under Bank of England limits
fields: Fnality UK Limited; Bank of England

The Bank's own classification, and it controls over any marketing language. The scaling gate is a supervisory permission, not a technical milestone — one regulator's decision stands between this and the whole "central-bank money on chain" pitch.

rows.title: Stripe completes its acquisition of Bridge
fields: The merchant-payments giant pulls stablecoin orchestration inside the house. Wallet infrastructure (Privy), a proprietary chain (Tempo) and a proposed trust bank follow. The pattern of the whole era in one deal: buy the missing layer, do not build a coalition.

rows.title: Kinexys, Chainlink and Ondo complete a cross-chain delivery-versus-payment test
fields: Ondo's tokenized Treasuries formed the asset leg; **J.P. Morgan deposits** formed the payment leg. A transaction path was proved. A production service was not.

rows.title: Fiserv announces FIUSD
fields: A stablecoin marketed into the core banking and merchant systems Fiserv already runs. Thirteen months later the public record still does not name the issuer, the redemption obligor or the reserve custodian. A coin with no stated debtor is not yet a coin.

rows.title: Digital Asset raises $135 million
fields: Digital Asset; DRW; Tradeweb; DTCC; Goldman Sachs; Citadel Securities; BNP Paribas; Circle Ventures; Paxos; Virtu

The dealers, the market makers, the banks, **the depository itself**, and the crypto firms all buy into the company that builds Canton. When DTCC is an investor in the ledger that will carry DTC's tokens, "disruption" is not the word for what is happening.

rows.title: Ripple and the SEC dismiss their appeals; the judgment stands
fields: Ripple Labs; SEC; U.S. District Court (S.D.N.Y.)

The district court's final judgment survives: a **$125,035,150** civil penalty and an injunction against unregistered institutional offers and sales. The long war ends not in vindication but in a paid fine and a standing injunction — and Ripple turns immediately toward the charter.

rows.title: NYDFS fines Paxos $26.5 million over the Binance relationship
fields: A $26.5M penalty plus $22M of mandated compliance investment, for historic anti-money-laundering and transaction-monitoring failures around the BUSD partnership. The lesson the sweep draws is the one that matters: **a regulated issuer can keep its reserves perfectly and still fail at watching its distributor.** Backing is not oversight.

rows.title: Anchorage files a Federal Reserve access request
fields: Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.; Federal Reserve

Tier 3. It is the most advanced request in the entire cohort, filed by the only member with a five-year-old national charter. **As of the Fed database's currency date of 2026-05-31 it is still pending** — nine months, no answer, no denial. This single line is the whole private stack's position in one fact.

rows.title: Fnality closes a $136 million Series C
fields: Fnality International; WisdomTree; Bank of America; Citi; KBC; Temasek; Tradeweb; Santander; Barclays; BNP Paribas; DTCC; Euroclear; Goldman Sachs; ING; Nasdaq Ventures; State Street; UBS
Twenty-four institutions. The money is not betting on a token; it is betting on the one rail that touches a central bank's balance sheet.

rows.title: Chainlink becomes a Canton Super Validator
fields: Chainlink Labs; Canton Network; Canton Foundation

The neutral connector takes a governance seat on the network it connects. The middleware vendor is now a governed market participant with a vote. The sweep flags the conflict plainly; nobody has resolved it.

rows.title: Deutsche Bank completes the first live euro cross-border payment on Partior
fields: Real money, real corridor. Each settlement bank still issues its own liability — the ledger is shared, the debt is not.

rows.title: Ripple closes the Hidden Road acquisition; it becomes Ripple Prime
fields: $1.25 billion for a prime brokerage. With Metaco and Standard Custody (custody), Rail (payments) and GTreasury (corporate treasury), Ripple has bought itself an end-to-end institutional money circuit. What it still does not have is an account at the Federal Reserve.

rows.title: Paxos announces the acquisition of Fordefi
fields: Institutional wallet and custody infrastructure, pulled inside. The missing layer, bought rather than built — again.

rows.title: DTCC and Euroclear become co-chairs of the Canton Foundation
fields: The incumbent depositories do not merely connect to the new network. They take the chair of the body that governs it.

rows.title: Anchorage's USAT issuance policies take effect
fields: The reserves sit in a segregated **South Dakota express trust** — legally separate from the OCC-chartered bank whose name is on the coin. Even inside one brand, the obligor is a different body from the bank.

rows.title: The OCC conditionally approves five digital-asset trust banks in a single day
fields: OCC; Circle / First National Digital Currency Bank; Ripple National Trust Bank; BitGo; Fidelity Digital Assets; Paxos

Five charters, one day, one agency — **the same agency that chartered the National Banks in 1863**. Conditional approval is not final approval, and final approval is not an open bank: each of the five must still satisfy pre-opening conditions, and each must separately apply for Federal Reserve Bank stock, which is a membership step and not an account.

rows.title: Paxos Trust Company, N.A. — conversion effective at 5:00 p.m.
fields: The New York limited-purpose trust becomes a national trust bank at a stated hour — one of the very few births in this corpus that carries a clock. Not FDIC insured. No deposits. Expected to apply for Federal Reserve Bank stock. Marketed as "GENIUS-ready"; what is actually true is the conversion.

rows.title: DTCC and Digital Asset announce a DTC Treasury-token path on Canton
fields: DTCC; DTC; Cede & Co.; Digital Asset; Canton Network

The design, read carefully, is the opposite of the headline. The conventional position is **immobilised** in a Digital Omnibus Account; the securities stay registered to **Cede & Co.**; DTC mints token *representations* of participant entitlements and treats its LedgerScan record as **part of DTC's own official books**. Settlement is not digitised at launch. The chain is a transport surface. Title never leaves the building.

rows.title: The Canton working group demonstrates a cross-border multi-asset repo
fields: Canton Network; LSEG Digital Settlement House; European government bonds; U.S. Treasuries

European government bonds and U.S. Treasuries against euro and dollar cash, including **tokenized commercial-bank deposits** supplied through LSEG. Staged, real assets, working-group only — not an open market. Collateral is where the new stack becomes load-bearing, and this is what the frontier actually looks like.

rows.title: BitGo Holdings lists on the NYSE
fields: The custodian becomes a public company six weeks after its charter conversion is approved. Capital follows permission.

rows.title: Ripple receives a full Electronic Money Institution licence in Luxembourg
fields: The European door opens before the American one. Note what it is and is not: an EMI licence is not a bank charter, and Ripple's own aggregate count of "75+ licences globally" should never be read as 75 bank charters.

rows.title: The OCC terminates Anchorage's 2021 operating agreement
fields: The bank is found compliant with all ten actionable articles; the corrective actions are judged effective and sustainable. **The charter is not terminated — the leash is.** A supervisory release, and a real one. It changes nothing about the Federal Reserve request still sitting in the queue.

rows.title: Bridge National Trust Bank receives preliminary conditional approval
fields: Stripe's stablecoin arm asks for a national trust charter and gets a conditional yes. The letter is explicit: pre-opening conditions must be met, the proposed bank **must apply for Federal Reserve Bank stock**, and none of this confirms a master account or authority to commence business.

rows.title: The federal banking agencies clarify capital treatment for tokenized securities
fields: Tokenized securities generally take the **same capital treatment as the non-tokenized form**. A technical clarification, not a product approval — and precisely the kind of quiet ruling that lets an incumbent adopt the new wrapper without changing anything else.

rows.title: Mastercard and SoFi announce they will explore SoFiUSD settlement
fields: "Explore." Settlement, Multi-Token Network support and Galileo distribution are all described as *expected*, not completed. The verb is the whole story.

rows.title: zerohash applies for a national trust bank charter
fields: An application, not an approval. As of the cutoff, no OCC decision has been located. zerohash already powers Morgan Stanley's E*Trade, Interactive Brokers Europe and a dozen other brands **without its name appearing anywhere the customer can see it** — which is exactly why its charter matters more than its profile.

rows.title: Mastercard agrees to acquire BVNK for up to $1.8 billion
fields: The card network buys the adapter — enterprise fiat-to-stablecoin conversion and treasury orchestration — rather than building a coin. It integrates at the layer where the choosing happens: which issuers, which chains, which banks, which liquidity venues get distribution. Signed, not closed.

rows.title: Coinbase National Trust Company receives preliminary conditional approval
fields: OCC; Coinbase Global; Coinbase National Trust Company
Conditional only. The letter states in terms that the proposed trust has **no authority to commence business** until final approval. Coinbase did not open a national bank; Coinbase got in line.

rows.title: Broadridge invests in HQLAx and announces a Canton migration path
fields: Broadridge; Digital Asset; HQLAx; Canton Network

The production repo platform ties itself more tightly to the collateral registry and to Canton. Custody, settlement and migration milestones all remain future work — the investment is real, the plumbing is a plan.

rows.title: J.P. Morgan's deposit token goes live on a public chain
fields: J.P. Morgan Chase Bank, N.A.; Kinexys; JPM Coin / JPMD; Base

The bank exports a **commercial-bank deposit liability** onto a public network for eligible institutional clients — while keeping the deposit claim, the compliance perimeter, the client relationship and the ledger inside the bank. Native Canton issuance remains a planned 2026 path, not a verified production fact. This is the sharpest single answer to "who keeps the gate."

rows.title: Visa reports a $7 billion annualized stablecoin settlement run rate
fields: Nine chains, 130+ stablecoin-linked card programmes, 50+ countries, up 50% quarter on quarter. **Visa-defined programme metrics, not audited totals** — and not one gram of membership, netting, fraud or dispute authority has moved. The settlement asset became pluggable. The rulebook did not.

rows.title: Paxos and BitGo appear on the OCC's active trust-bank list
fields: OCC; Paxos Trust Company, N.A. (charter 25379); BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. (charter 25366)
Consummated. Two of the five December charters are now operating national trust banks with charter numbers. Neither has a confirmed Federal Reserve master account.

rows.title: DTCC and Chainlink collaborate on 24/7 collateral management
fields: The Collateral AppChain is a *third* object — not DTC's entitlement-token service, not the Stellar connection. They may become interoperable. They do not share a ledger, a validator set, a legal operator, a cash asset or a rulebook merely because DTCC is in all three.

rows.title: The SEC grants Paxos Securities Settlement Company temporary clearing-agency registration
fields: SEC; Paxos Securities Settlement Company, LLC (PSSC)

rows.title: SoFiUSD launches — the first stablecoin issued by a U.S. national bank
fields: The one clean vertical in the whole sweep: charter-holder, issuer and consumer brand are the same body. And the coin it issues **is not an insured deposit**. An FDIC-insured national bank can hand you two dollars with entirely different rights attached, and nothing at the counter tells you which one you are holding.

rows.title: DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation announce a planned connection
The Federal Reserve access database: Anchorage still pending
fields: Federal Reserve; Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.

The currency date of the public request database. Anchorage's request, filed nine months earlier, remains **pending**. No other member of the cohort has a publicly confirmed master account. The record shows a full waiting room and an unopened door.

rows.title: FIUSD production target ("summer 2026")
fields: Slipped once already, from year-end 2025. The issuer, the redemption obligor, the reserve custodian and the first production users all remain unnamed in public documentation. Watch for a named debtor — until there is one, there is no coin.

rows.title: MoneyGram launches MGUSD on Stellar
fields: MoneyGram; Bridge (issuer of record); M0; Fireblocks
MoneyGram is the face. **Bridge** — which is Stripe — is the regulated issuer of record. M0 supplies the mint-and-burn logic. Three companies deep before you find out whose promise you are holding.

rows.title: Mastercard expands settlement across multiple stablecoins and chains
fields: Mastercard; Circle (USDC); Paxos (PYUSD, USDG, USDP); Ripple (RLUSD); SoFi (SoFiUSD)

Five issuers, eight chains — and Mastercard's fraud rules, dispute rules, participant structure and rulebook entirely intact. USDC carried early live flows; most of the rest was support and rollout, not proven volume. The network adopts tokenized cash **without yielding the customer or the constitution**.

rows.title: Ripple reports RLUSD at $1.576 billion against $1.683 billion of reserves
fields: Ripple; Standard Custody & Trust Company; RLUSD

Monthly CPA attestations, over-collateralised on the company's own numbers. A real regulated coin with a real reserve — issued by a **New York limited-purpose trust company**, not by the national bank Ripple has been conditionally approved to build.

rows.title: DTC's preliminary tokenization service (stated window: second half of 2026)
fields: DTC; DTCC; Canton Network; Cede & Co.

The December press release said the first half of 2026; DTC's own FAQ quietly moved it to the second half. **This lands in the same six months as the Treasury clearing mandate.** Watch the eligible CUSIPs, the first participant, the first transfer, the cash leg, and the correction path — the day a mistaken transfer must be undone is the day the new stack says out loud which ledger wins.

rows.title: Swift says its blockchain ledger is ready for initial use
fields: Swift; ANZ; BNP Paribas; BNY; Citi; DBS; HSBC; Lloyds; MUFG; Standard Chartered; UBS; Wells Fargo (17 banks in total)

Seventeen of the world's largest banks lined up to pilot — and what the ledger carries is **bank-issued tokenized deposits**, not public stablecoins. Final settlement still completes through the existing systems. The correspondent-banking guild did not surrender the rail. It built one, and kept the rulebook, the identity layer and the message standard it already owned.

rows.title: Circle receives final OCC approval
fields: OCC; Circle Internet Group; First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. (Circle National Trust)

The first **final** — not conditional — approval in the cohort. And the gap that remains is the point: the opening date is unconfirmed, the transfer of reserve management is a planned future step, and **there is no confirmed Federal Reserve account**. Even the furthest-advanced charter in America has daylight between "final approval" and "open for business."

rows.title: Custodia files its cert petition at the Supreme Court
fields: Custodia Bank; Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City; Supreme Court of the United States

The Wyoming special-purpose depository institution takes the master-account question to the highest court. Fourteen chartered or approved bodies are standing in the same queue behind it. **This is no longer one bank's lawsuit — it is the load-bearing case of the entire private monetary stack.**

rows.title: The wider OCC queue: a dozen more applicants nobody is naming
fields: OCC; World Liberty Trust Company; PAYO Digital Bank; zerohash national trust bank; Revolut Bank US; EDX Trust; Bastion Platforms; Lorum National Trust Bank; OpenReserve Bank; Agora National Trust Bank; Catena Trust Bank; Payward National Trust Company; CBW Bank

The famous names are the visible part. The OCC's public digital-asset application list holds a far longer queue — a president's family venture, a British neobank, an exchange consortium, and a row of trust companies almost nobody has heard of. **A charter application is not an operating bank; a conditional approval is not a final one; and a trust charter is neither deposit insurance nor a Federal Reserve account.** The queue is the story.

rows.title: Kraken's claimed Federal Reserve account is not in the public record
fields: Payward; Kraken Bank (Wyoming SPDI); Federal Reserve

Kraken's group **states** that its Wyoming special-purpose depository holds a limited-purpose Federal Reserve account. The Fed's public access database does not corroborate it under any known Kraken or Payward name. Either Kraken is the first crypto-adjacent body through the door in American history, or the claim inflated in the telling. **Unconfirmed, and checkable** — which makes it a watch, not a finding.

rows.title: The Ripple master-account claim is a conflation
fields: Ripple; Standard Custody & Trust Company; Federal Reserve; OCC

The OCC's conditional-approval letter says the *proposed* Ripple National Trust Bank will apply for **Federal Reserve Bank stock** — a membership step. That is not a master-account request, and no Ripple or Standard Custody request was found in the Fed's public database. Membership, stock, a reserve account and a confirmed master account are four different things, and the retail story treats them as one.

rows.title: Coinbase International Exchange consolidates into Deribit
fields: Positions and balances migrate, subject to readiness and approvals. Global derivatives liquidity and risk concentrate into a single venue. Watch the legal novations, the risk-engine cutover and the insurance-fund treatment — concentration is only invisible until it isn't.

rows.title: DTCC's Collateral AppChain (target: fourth quarter 2026)
fields: A separate object from the tokenization service. Watch asset eligibility, valuation, margin, the cash leg, and whether any of it carries production volume.

rows.title: Mastercard's BVNK acquisition — outer bound of the stated closing window
fields: "Before year-end 2026." Until it closes, BVNK is a separate company. Watch the surviving legal entities, the licences, the safeguarding banks — and whether BVNK stays asset-neutral once a card network owns it.

rows.title: DTC-tokenized assets on Stellar (target: first half of 2027)
fields: Watch the first eligible asset, the authoritative-record design, the cash leg, the corporate actions — and whether XLM has any role at all beyond paying for network function.

rows.title: PSSC's temporary clearing registration reaches its outer limit
fields: SEC; Paxos Securities Settlement Company, LLC

Eighteen months from the grant of 2026-05-27. Unless the Commission acts, the permission lapses. Watch permanent registration, scope changes, DTC membership — and the first default or recovery procedure, which is where a settlement system stops being a press release.

rows.title: Executive Order: Independent Agencies Answer to the White House — Except Fed Monetary Policy
fields: The order pulling independent agencies under White House review carves out the Fed's conduct of monetary policy but keeps its supervision and regulation of banks inside the fence. The seam is drawn deliberately: the money lever stays nominally independent, the bank-oversight lever does not.
executive order, Fed independence, supervision, independent agencies

rows.title: Sony Files for a US Trust Bank (Connectia) — the Bank Lobby Objects
fields: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

Sony Financial Group's Connectia Trust applies for a national trust charter to issue a stablecoin and custody crypto; BPI, ICBA and NCRC all file to urge rejection. A Japanese electronics conglomerate at the gate of the US banking system, with the incumbent lobby holding the door.
Sony, Connectia, trust charter, BPI opposition, stablecoin

rows.title: OCC RFI on Community Banks and Their Core Service Providers
fields: Treasury Department — Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

The OCC asks how community banks' dependence on a handful of core technology providers affects their ability to compete in a rapidly evolving market — explicitly naming the growing stablecoin and crypto-asset markets. The question beneath the question: can small banks even reach the new rails, or will the gate favor the giants?
community banks, core service providers, stablecoin, competition, OCC

rows.title: Request for Information and Comment on Reserve Bank Payment Account Prototype
fields: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) seeks public input on a special purpose Reserve Bank account prototype (a Payment Account) tailored to the risks and needs of institutions focused on payments innovation. A Payment Account holder would be expected to use its account for the express purpose of clearing and settling the institution's payment activity. Payment Accounts would be designed to pose limited risk to the Federal Reserve Banks (Reserve Banks) and the overall payment system, and Reserve Banks would generally conduct a streamlined review of requests for these accounts. Any institution that is legally eligible for Federal Reserve accounts or services (accounts and services) under the Federal Reserve Act would be eligible to request a Payment Account from a Reserve Bank. The Payment Account protype does not seek to expand or otherwise change legal eligibility for access to accounts and services.

rows.title: World Liberty Trust Company Files for a National Charter — the President's Family at the OCC's Door
fields: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

World Liberty Financial — the Trump family's stablecoin venture (USD1) — files for a national trust bank charter. The application sits pending on the OCC's own digital-assets licensing table through the Freedom 250 year: the ruling family asking the executive's own regulator for a bank.
World Liberty, Trump family, trust charter, USD1, OCC queue

rows.title: Proposal to Codify Removal of “Reputation Risk” from Bank Supervision
fields: Following earlier actions, the Board requests comment on codifying the removal of reputational risk as a basis for supervisory action — the formal unwinding of the debanking / “Operation Chokepoint” posture that had kept crypto and other disfavored businesses off the banking rails.
reputation risk, debanking, Operation Chokepoint, supervision

rows.title: Prohibition on Use of Reputation Risk or Other Supervisory Tools To Encourage or Compel Banking Organizations To Engage in Politicized or Unlawful Discrimination
fields: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board) is inviting public comment on a notice of proposed rulemaking (proposal or proposed rule) that would codify the removal of reputation risk from the Board's supervisory programs. The proposal would prohibit the Board from encouraging or compelling Board-supervised banking organizations to deny or condition the provision of banking or other financial products or services to an individual or business based on their constitutionally protected political or religious beliefs, associations, speech, or conduct, or based on involvement by the individual or business in politically disfavored but lawful business activities perceived to present reputation risk.

rows.title: FSOC Raises the Bar for Calling Anything Systemic
fields: The council rewrites its nonbank designation framework, raising the conditions for designation. Just as stablecoin issuers, tokenized collateral networks, and new clearinghouses wire into the system, the tool for naming a nonbank systemically important gets harder to use.

rows.title: Treasury Guts the OFR — the Eyes of FSOC Dim
fields: Staffing and organizational cuts hit the Office of Financial Research, the Dodd-Frank body that supplies FSOC's data and analysis. The watchtower is thinned in the middle of the biggest plumbing rebuild since 1934. Whoever keeps the data keeps the sight.

rows.title: Treasury Rewrites CDFI Compliance — the Community-Credit Gate Moves
fields: Changes to CDFI program compliance touch who qualifies and what public benefits count. Small next to the clearing mandate, but the same motion: the federal gates on who may access credit and certification, being re-hung one by one.

rows.title: Prohibition on the Use of Reputation Risk by Regulators
fields: Treasury Department — Comptroller of the Currency

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation are adopting a final rule to codify the elimination of reputation risk from their supervisory programs. Among other things, the rule prohibits the agencies from criticizing or taking adverse action against an institution on the basis of reputation risk. The rule also prohibits the agencies from requiring, instructing, or encouraging an institution to close an account, to refrain from providing an account, product, or service, or to modify or terminate any product or service on the basis of a person or entity's political, social, cultural, or religious views or beliefs, constitutionally protected speech, or solely on the basis of politically disfavored but lawful business activities perceived to present reputation risk. The rule further forbids the agencies from taking any supervisory action or other adverse action against an institution, a group of institutions, or the institution-affiliated parties of any institution that is designed to punish or discourage an individual or group from engaging in any lawful political, social, cultural, or religious activities, constitutionally protected speech, or, for political reasons, lawful business activities that the agencies or its personnel disagree with or disfavor.

rows.title: Kraken Files for a National Trust Charter — Two Months After Its Master Account
fields: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

Payward (Kraken), already the first crypto firm ever granted a Fed master account (Kansas City Fed, March 4), files for a national trust company charter. Access to the rails, then a federal charter to stand on: the Custodia dream realized by its Wyoming neighbor, on the Fed's terms.
Kraken, Payward, trust charter, master account, SPDI

rows.title: KC Fed Frames Kraken Account as Payment-Account Pilot
fields: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

The Kansas City Fed published a supplemental document framing the Kraken Financial limited-purpose account (granted March 4, 2026) as a pilot of the Reserve Bank payment-account concept — the first live test of the prototype the Board proposed in FR 2026-10375. Only overdraft-rejecting services (Fedwire Funds) are available; neither the Kraken exchange nor other Payward subsidiaries get access. The pilot generates real-world data for the payment-account rulebook whose comment period closes July 27, 2026.
Kraken, payment account, pilot, master account, gate, Kansas City Fed, Fedwire

rows.title: OCC Interpretive Letter 1192: State Money-Transmitter Laws and the National Charter
fields: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

The sleeper letter on the applicability of state money-transmitter licensing — preemption of fifty state regimes is precisely what makes a national trust charter worth having for a payments firm. The quiet legal engine under the whole charter wave.
IL 1192, preemption, money transmitter, trust charter

rows.title: Regulation D — Master Accounts vs. Special-Purpose Payment Accounts
fields: Amends Regulation D to carve out a new category of “Payment Accounts” distinct from full master accounts, and to deny them interest on balances held at the Fed. Commenters warned that widely adopted dollar stablecoins could displace non-interest currency and erode the Fed's low-cost funding base — the central bank protecting its seat as the stablecoin era arrives.
master account, Payment Account, interest on reserves, stablecoin, Regulation D

rows.title: Regulation A — No Discount-Window Access for Payment Accounts
fields: Amends Regulation A to specify that holders of the new special-purpose Payment Accounts would NOT be eligible for discount-window credit. Combined with prefunding and no-overdraft rules, this fences the new entrants off from the Fed's lender-of-last-resort backstop — onto the rails, but without the safety net.
discount window, Payment Account, lender of last resort, Regulation A

rows.title: Proposed Revisions to the Policy on Payment System Risk and the Account Access Guidelines
fields: The Board proposes a new Part IV of the Payment System Risk policy to create special-purpose “Payment Accounts” at the Reserve Banks, and revises the guidelines for who may access Reserve Bank accounts and services. Critically, it encourages Reserve Banks to PAUSE decisions on account requests from Tier 3 (riskiest, novel-charter) institutions until the policy is finished — the master-account gate, written into policy.
master account, account access, Payment Account, Tier 3, Custodia, PSR policy

rows.title: The Community Banks Ask Kansas City to Take Kraken's Account Back
fields: ICBA formally asks the Kansas City Fed to review immediately whether Kraken Financial's limited-purpose account squares with the account-access guidelines — and to weigh additional limits, suspension, non-renewal, or termination. Its evidence: ICIJ reporting that Kraken moved at least $1.1B in Bitcoin to crypto-ATM operators. The account runs on a one-year term; the letter builds the public record for the first renewal (~March 2027). The first organized push to close the one door a district opened.
Kraken, master account, gate, ICBA, Kansas City Fed

rows.title: NCUA Final Rule: Prohibition on the Use of Reputation Risk
fields: First agency to write the debanking ban into regulation: examiners may no longer use 'reputation risk' to lean on institutions, implementing EO 14331 (Guaranteeing Fair Banking). The agency stopped examining for it in September 2025; this makes the removal permanent — the anti-debanking agenda hardening from policy into law.
reputation risk, debanking, NCUA, EO 14331, fair banking

rows.title: Federal Reserve AML/CFT Program Proposed Rule (Docket R-1835)
fields: Board of Governors, Federal Reserve System

Proposed rule requiring Fed-supervised banks to establish risk-based AML/CFT programs, aligned with FinCEN's AML Act of 2020 implementation and parallel OCC/FDIC/NCUA changes. Comments due Sep 8, 2026. Doc 2026-13919. This was the Fed's AML rewrite flagged in the 07-08 sweep — now formally published.
AML, CFT, Federal Reserve, proposed rule, Bank Secrecy Act

rows.title: Kraken Financial's CEO Testifies to Wyoming's Blockchain Committee About Its Fed Account
fields: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

Kraken Financial CEO Brian Mathena testified to Wyoming's Select Committee on Blockchain, Financial Technology and Digital Innovation at its July 14-15, 2026 meeting; the official minutes record that he highlighted receipt of a Federal Reserve master account.
Kraken, master account, Tier 3, Kansas City Fed, Bowman, Dart Bank, Wyoming

rows.title: SIPA customer-property liquidation route
fields: Recover or resolve a failed institution
A financially troubled SIPC-member broker-dealer has missing customer cash or securities and a SIPA liquidation is applicable.
Securities Investor Protection Act and the liquidation case.
Confirm SIPC-member broker-dealer status and the statutory trigger.
Establish customer status, asset classification, account facts, and claim deadlines.
Apply SIPA's limits and the trustee/court process.
SIPC is distinct from FDIC deposit insurance; it does not protect market-value loss, ordinary investment losses, commodities/FX claims, or digital/crypto assets outside SIPA's security definition.

rows.title: Federal bankruptcy court and estate-administration route
fields: Recover or resolve a failed institution
An eligible debtor's insolvency is governed by the Bankruptcy Code rather than a specialized bank, broker-dealer, insurer, or other resolution regime.
Bankruptcy Code eligibility and the applicable chapter/court process.
Identify the exact debtor legal entity and its eligibility.
Identify the chapter, venue, court orders, estate fiduciary, and property/claim characterization.
Test whether a specialized insolvency, receivership, or resolution statute applies instead.
Debtors in possession where the Bankruptcy Code permits

Bankruptcy is not a catch-all: domestic banks are excluded by section 109, and specialized regimes can govern other regulated entities. A token ledger does not by itself identify estate property, perfection, custody, or priority.

rows.title: Covered clearing-agency recovery and wind-down planning route
fields: Recover or resolve a failed institution
A covered SEC-registered clearing agency is within Rule 17Ad-22's applicable recovery and orderly-wind-down requirements.
Exchange Act clearing-agency framework and SEC Rule 17Ad-22.
Identify the registered clearing agency and whether it is covered by the cited provisions.
Recover the current recovery/wind-down plan, default rules, liquidity arrangements, and participant obligations.
Apply the exact service, product, member, and event rather than an organization-wide label.
Default-management and recovery-plan actors named by an effective clearing-agency rulebook
A recovery plan is not an observed resolution outcome, a customer guarantee, or a universal default waterfall for broker-dealers, banks, custodians, issuers, or blockchain networks.

sections.title: Fourteen requirements in three groups
sections.sub: A technology qualifies only for a particular function inside a particular legal and transaction path. The end-to-end route remains constrained by its weakest indispensable join.
sections.home: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/TRANSITION_GATES_2026-09-22.json
sections.part: 4 · Transition gates: where a technology qualifies, and where it does not

rows.title: Functional fit
fields: Can the technology perform this exact job?

rows.title: Legal seat
fields: Which exact entity is authorized or appointed?

rows.title: Exact route
fields: Which product, contract, network and transaction use it?

rows.title: Operating receipt
fields: What funded event proves the function operated?

rows.title: Scale and stress
fields: Did it recur, survive failure and permit retirement?

rows.title: Core candidate
fields: Can perform the central function, subject to the exact legal and operating route.

rows.title: Conditional candidate
fields: Relevant capability exists, but deployment, rights, access or operating fit remains unresolved.

rows.title: Supporting layer
fields: Supplies a necessary control or service without owning the core function.

rows.title: Outside this function
fields: Performs a different job; adjacency does not make it a candidate for this requirement.

rows.title: Constitute the transaction
fields: Define the claim, actors, ownership, mandate and code authority.

rows.title: Make value move
fields: Govern trading, clearing, liquidity, final money and stablecoin claims.

rows.title: Close and survive
fields: Service the asset, close the books, interoperate, correct failure and retire duplication.

rows.title: Legally defined claim
fields: What is the digital object, who owes it and how is it created, transferred and extinguished?
Exact issuer, governing instrument, effective legal perimeter and authoritative product terms.
A ledger can carry a representation without defining the external legal claim.
Issuer law, Governing instrument, Product terms, Authoritative record
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 product-specific · Note: Named regulated entities can constitute and record exact securities or fund interests where appointed.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 issuer component · Note: The applicable Circle entity defines the USDC issuer claim and redemption terms.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R2-R4 by object · Note: RLUSD has an issuer claim; XRPL and XRP do not inherit that claim definition.
Fit: core · Maturity: R3 bounded path · Note: DTC rules define the reviewed tokenized participant entitlement inside the incumbent depository structure.
Fit: core · Maturity: R1-R4 by claim · Note: Deposits, deposit tokens, stablecoins and central-bank money each require a different obligor and rule set.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R2-R4 by product · Note: Legal vehicles can define product claims; Base or token possession does not do so alone.
Fit: core · Maturity: R2-R4 by product · Note: The U.S. structure separates the security, custodian, transfer agent and token state.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 bank claim · Note: JPM Coin represents a commercial-bank deposit claim of the issuing bank.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 non-U.S. product · Note: The token defines a contractual backed exposure, not issuer-register common stock.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 non-U.S. product · Note: The product claims mirrored economic rights; equivalence to the underlying share remains bounded.

rows.title: Accountable actors
fields: Which exact legal entities occupy the issuer, venue, custody, record, settlement and recovery seats?
Effective authorization, appointment or membership for the exact entity and function.
A brand, affiliate, foundation, validator or software project does not inherit another entity's permission.
License or charter, Appointment, Membership, Enforceable duties
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 product-specific · Note: Its transfer-agent, broker/ATS, advisory and administration entities occupy distinct seats.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 issuer component · Note: Exact Circle issuer and service entities can be tied to specific duties.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 incumbent / R3 token path · Note: DTC is the regulated operator; DTCC parent and Cede perform different roles.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 by entity · Note: Exchange, custody, network and tokenization vehicles retain separate entity perimeters.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R2-R4 by entity · Note: Ripple products and controlled entities can occupy seats; XRPL and XRP do not become those entities.
Fit: core · Maturity: R3 bounded path · Note: Swift and participant banks can be identified separately in the coordination route.
Fit: core · Maturity: R1-R2 · Note: The temporary clearing-agency registration identifies a bounded legal operator before operation.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 ATS comparator · Note: The ATS supplies a named venue entity under its existing legal route.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 custody component · Note: Anchorage and BitGo illustrate exact custody entities and key-control duties.

rows.title: Ownership, control and priority
fields: Which record controls ownership, and how are custody, liens, customer property and insolvency resolved?
Controlling record rule, custody and segregation terms, perfected interest and applicable insolvency treatment.
Wallet control, a token account or possession of a key does not alone establish beneficial ownership or priority.
State property law, UCC control, Custody books, Bankruptcy regime
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 product-specific · Note: Transfer-agent and composite record models can control title for exact products.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 incumbent / R3 token path · Note: Cede, DTC participant and customer entitlement tiers remain distinct.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 tooling · Note: Key policy and contract restrictions can support control without deciding legal ownership.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 custody component · Note: Custody and segregation can protect assets but do not define the issuer's register.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R2-R4 by product · Note: Custody and legal-register vehicles vary by product; token possession is not enough.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R1-R2 · Note: The registered CSD/settlement design may control specified positions once operating.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R2-R4 by product · Note: Custodial NMS-security entitlement differs from issuer-register ownership.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 non-U.S. product · Note: One-for-one backing does not make the holder the underlying issuer's shareholder.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 non-U.S. product · Note: Custodial brokerage holdings and token-level rights require product-specific priority analysis.

rows.title: Human and machine authority
fields: Who authorized the instruction, within what limits, and who bears liability when an agent exceeds them?
Enforceable mandate plus tested authorization, denial, revocation and human escalation.
A valid signature proves use of a credential, not necessarily legal authority, purpose or compliance.
Principal-agent mandate, Credential binding, Limits and revocation, Liability rule
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 tooling / mandate unproved · Note: Policy engines and identity-aware contracts can encode signing and transfer limits.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 account capability · Note: Account authorization can change cryptographic authority; legal mandate and whole-route controls remain external.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 execution · Note: Wallet and contract permissions can enforce technical limits but do not create agency authority.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 execution · Note: Program and account authority can constrain actions while legal capacity remains separate.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 platform controls · Note: Account, custody and transaction controls can authenticate users within the product perimeter.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R3 bounded path · Note: Bank instruction and participant frameworks can identify institutional authority; autonomous-agent scope remains unproved.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 custody controls · Note: Wallet policy and movement authorization support the mandate but do not define the principal's legal intent.

rows.title: Smart-contract constitution
fields: Who deploys, upgrades, pauses, corrects and terminates the code—and what happens when code and law diverge?
Exact code identity, audit, administrator and key governance, legal terms, oracle responsibility and tested correction.
Base-layer finality does not allocate responsibility for a bug, bad oracle, fork or irreversible loss.
Governing terms, Admin-key control, Oracle duty, Emergency and wind-down rules
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 execution · Note: General-purpose public smart-contract execution; application governance remains external.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 execution · Note: Live public runtime and token programs can carry exact application rules.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 execution · Note: Asset and payment operations can encode bounded issuer and transfer controls.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 execution · Note: Live execution and account primitives can implement the technical control surface.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 network / route-specific · Note: XRPL can execute asset and payment functions; the relevant contract and administrator vary by product.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 network · Note: Native services and council governance offer an institutional control surface; application authority stays separate.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 network · Note: Custom L1s can choose validators and permissions; exact operator and failure rules must be named.
Fit: core · Maturity: R3-R4 institutional · Note: Permissioned application workflows can encode synchronized performance across domains.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 middleware · Note: Oracle and messaging services can trigger code but require responsibility for data and delivery failures.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 middleware · Note: Cross-chain messaging can connect contracts without governing their legal effect.
Fit: supporting · Maturity: R4 tooling · Note: ERC-3643 and custody controls can add pause, recovery and identity-aware transfer rules.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R2-R4 by design · Note: Execution contracts can automate matching or liquidity but require a regulated operating constitution.
Fit: outside · Maturity: R4 native transfer · Note: The base design provides native transfer and script constraints, not the general application-control surface used by this requirement.

rows.title: Governed trading and price formation
fields: Who operates the venue, admits assets and participants, surveils abuse and handles bad trades and halts?
Operating lawful venue, admitted assets, transaction data, surveillance and exercised halt or error procedures.
A DEX, AMM contract or public price does not itself supply the regulated operator or customer protections.
Venue authority, Asset admission, Market surveillance, Halt and error rules
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 ATS component · Note: Securitize Markets can operate product-specific access and trading functions.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 ATS comparator · Note: The ATS is an operating venue comparator but is not a TSV by implication.
Fit: core · Maturity: R4 platform / product-specific · Note: Regulated market entities and product vehicles vary across the stack.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R2-R4 by deployment · Note: AMM and solver designs can perform execution but do not supply the regulated venue or surveillance.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 execution / R1 TSV route · Note: A core public-chain candidate for the SEC venue design, subject to every legal and product condition.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 execution / R1 TSV route · Note: A core technical candidate; no operating TSV selection is established.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 execution / R1 TSV route · Note: A core technical candidate for the order's public-chain surface, not an approved venue.
Fit: conditional · Maturity: R4 execution / R1 TSV route · Note: A core technical candidate; the exact venue, assets and liquidity remain unproved.

rows.title: Trump v. Cook — SCOTUS No. 25A312; below D.D.C. and D.C. Circuit
fields: Trump v. Cook — SCOTUS No. 25A312; below D.D.C. and D.C. Circuit
May the President immediately remove a sitting Fed Governor "for cause," without notice and a chance to answer — and is the Governor's tenure protection constitutional?

Stay denied 2026-06-29 (Roberts for a 5-4 majority): courts may review 'cause', a removal needs notice and a chance to respond, and Cook stays in office while the case continues. On 2026-10-07 the President named a committee to decide whether cause exists; its hearing is set for 2026-11-05.
One Governor's chair is one FOMC vote — and the ruling drew the constitutional fence around the Fed itself: the one agency the removal revolution doesn't reach.

rows.title: Trump v. Slaughter — SCOTUS No. 25-332; below D.D.C.
fields: Trump v. Slaughter — SCOTUS No. 25-332; below D.D.C.
Does the FTC's for-cause removal protection survive Article II?
Reversed 6–3 on 2026-06-29: FTC protection unconstitutional; Humphrey's Executor no longer shields the modern commission. The Fed was expressly treated as a distinct historical arrangement.
Every independent financial commission except the Fed is now removable at will — the President's hand reaches SEC-style bodies, and only the central bank keeps its carve-out.

rows.title: Custodia Bank v. Federal Reserve Board & FRB Kansas City — D. Wyo.; 10th Cir. 24-8024; SCOTUS No. 26-62
fields: Custodia Bank v. Federal Reserve Board & FRB Kansas City — D. Wyo.; 10th Cir. 24-8024; SCOTUS No. 26-62
Does statutory eligibility give a state-chartered bank a right to a Reserve Bank master account?

Tenth Circuit (2025-10-31): eligibility for a master account is not an entitlement. Custodia petitioned the Supreme Court on 2026-07-10 (No. 26-62); the Fed opposed review on 2026-10-13. The Court has not yet decided whether to hear it.

THE gate case. Every crypto bank, fintech trust, and state money experiment needs the Fed's rails; whether access is a right or a favor is now before the Court — or settled for a generation if cert is denied.

rows.title: Banco San Juan Internacional v. FRBNY & Board — S.D.N.Y.; 2d Cir. 25-1144
fields: Banco San Juan Internacional v. FRBNY & Board — S.D.N.Y.; 2d Cir. 25-1144
May a Reserve Bank terminate an existing master account under contract and risk process?
Affirmed 2026-05-13: no statutory right to continued service; FRBNY's termination authority stands.
The gate swings both ways — an account once granted can be taken. Second and Tenth Circuits now converge on Reserve Bank discretion.

rows.title: Fourth Corner Credit Union v. FRB Kansas City — D. Colo.; 10th Cir. 16-1016 (2017)
fields: Fourth Corner Credit Union v. FRB Kansas City — D. Colo.; 10th Cir. 16-1016 (2017)
Must a Reserve Bank serve a state-chartered cannabis credit union?
Fractured 1-1-1 judgment; amended lawful-purpose complaint allowed; no entitlement established. Later Custodia law rejects the entitlement reading.
The first crack at the gate question — three judges, three theories, no rule — showing why Custodia's published holding matters.

rows.title: TNB USA v. FRBNY — S.D.N.Y. 1:18-cv-07978 (2020)
fields: Did FRBNY unlawfully stall a "narrow bank" built to pass interest-on-reserves to depositors?
Dismissed as unripe (2020) — no final denial, no merits ruling.
The narrow-bank idea — 100%-reserve money without lending — died in the waiting room, not in court. The gate can win by never answering.
